dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(ن، وَالْقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ) ن: the discussion of the i'rab of the openings of the surahs has been given before, and we add what al-Zamakhsharī said in refutation of those who strain the meaning. He said: This letter is one of the letters of the alphabet. As for their saying that it is the inkwell, I do not know whether that is a linguistic or a religious coinage. If it is a name for the inkwell, it must be either a generic noun or a proper name. If it is generic, where are the inflection and the tanwīn? If it is a proper name, where is the inflection? Whichever it is, it must have a position in the composition of the speech. If you say it is something sworn by, then if it is generic you must put it in the genitive and give it tanwīn, and the oath would be by an indefinite, unknown inkwell, as if it were said "by an inkwell and by the pen"; and if it is a proper name, you must make it triptote and put it in the genitive, or make it diptote and give it a fatḥa because of being a proper name and feminine. Likewise the interpretation as "the fish": either one of the fish (نون from النينان) is meant, or it is made a proper name for the Bahamūt that they claim; and likewise the interpretation as a tablet of light or of gold, and as the river in Paradise. Abū Ḥayyān affirmed that none of that is sound.
The wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, القلم is what is sworn by, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم (I swear). Allah the Exalted swore by the pen to magnify its matter and to extol its standing, and because of the benefits and advantages in it which no description can encompass; that is, what is meant by it is the genus of pen, comprising the pens with which one writes. The Exalted said: «وربك الأكرم الذي علّم بالقلم». And because one benefits from it as one benefits from speech; for this reason it is said: the pen is one of the two tongues. The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is relative or maṣdariyya; in any case it is conjoined to القلم. So He swore first by the pen, then by the angels' writing or by what they write. Thus the things sworn by are two, and the things sworn to are three: the negation of madness from him, the establishment of reward for him, and his being upon the tolerant ḥanīf religion. (ما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ) a clause with no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath. ما is the negating ما of the Ḥijāzīs; بنعمة ربك is attached to the meaning of negation indicated by ما, and the bāʾ is causal. The bāʾ [in بمجنون] is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and مجنون is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of ما. The meaning is: madness has been negated from you because of your Lord's bestowing favour on you with prophethood and other things. Further explanation of attaching the preposition with its genitive and the adverb to the meaning of negation will come in the section on benefits. (وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْراً غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ) the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause and what follows it are conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath, so both are part of what is sworn to, as stated just now. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, لك its fronted khabar, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), أجرا its subject, and غير ممنون a naʿt (adjective), i.e. not cut off. (وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ) إنّ and its subject, the shifted lām, على خلق the khabar and عظيم a naʿt. (فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ) the fāʾ is resumptive, the sīn a particle of the future, and تبصر an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is latent (mustatir), implied as أنت; يبصرون is conjoined to ستبصر. (بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ) the grammarians differed sharply over it, and we present the most preferred views, which are four: 1- that the bāʾ is added to the mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being أيّكم المفتون, so the bāʾ was added as it is added in بحسبك زيد; 2- that the bāʾ is in the sense of في, so it is locative, as in your saying "Zayd is بالبصرة", i.e. in it, and the meaning is: in which group and party of you is the one afflicted; 3- that it is by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "by which of you was the afflicted afflicted", so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, and the bāʾ is causal; 4- that المفتون is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came on the pattern mafʿūl, like المعقول and الميسور, the implied form being بأيّكم الفتون. In any case the clause is in the position of an accusative, governed by what precedes it, because that is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative particle. Further discussion on this matter will come in the section on benefits. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ) the clause has no grammatical position, because it gives the reason for what preceded, since what came before it announced the appearance of their madness such that it is hidden from no one. إنّ and its subject; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. You may parse هو as a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and أعلم as the khabar. بمن is attached to أعلم, the clause ضلّ is the ṣila (relative clause), and عن سبيله is attached to ضلّ. هو is a mubtadaʾ, أعلم the khabar, and بالمهتدين is attached to أعلم.

* Rhetoric:
From His words «ن والقلم وما يسطرون» to His words «غير ممنون» there is the device of verbal correspondence (al-munāsaba al-lafẓiyya), which consists in bringing words that are balanced in measure and rhymed.

* Benefits:
1- The majority of grammarians forbade attaching the preposition with its genitive and the adverb to particles of meaning; some of them permitted it, and some made a distinction, saying: if it stands in for an omitted verb, that is permissible by way of substitution, not originally; otherwise not. Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: Among that is the saying of the Exalted: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون — the bāʾ is attached to the negation, since if it were attached to مجنون it would convey the negation of a specific madness, namely the one that comes from Allah's favour, and there is no madness in existence that is a favour. This is what Ibn al-Ḥājib and others mentioned, and it is a marvellous statement, except that the majority of grammarians do not agree with the soundness of attachment to a particle; so on their view it should be implied that the attachment is to a verb indicated by the negator, i.e. "that was negated by your Lord's favour". I mentioned in my commentary on the ode of Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr, when discussing his saying:
وما سعاد غداة البين إذ رحلوا ... إلا أغن غضيض الطرف مكحول
(And Suʿād, on the morning of parting when they departed, was nothing but a soft-voiced gazelle with lowered, kohl-darkened eyes.)
that the preferred view is to attach the adverb to the meaning of comparison which the verse contains, on the basis that the original is "and nothing like Suʿād but a soft-voiced gazelle", by reversed comparison for hyperbole, so that the adverb would not, in the underlying form, precede the word carrying the meaning of comparison. And if it is permissible for the particle of comparison to govern the ḥāl (circumstantial) in such a case as his saying:
كأن قلوب الطير رطبا ويابسا ... لدى وكرها العناب والحشف البالي
(As if the hearts of the birds, fresh and dry, by its nest were jujubes and worn-out dry dates.)
even though the ḥāl resembles the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), then its governing the adverb is more fitting.
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he took a strange course in attaching بنعمة. He said: «If you say: to what is the bāʾ in بنعمة ربك attached, and what is its position? I say: it is attached to مجنون in the negative, just as it is attached to عاقل in the affirmative in your saying "you are, by Allah's favour, sane", affirmation and negation being equal in that, just as they are equal in your saying "Zayd struck ʿAmr" and "Zayd did not strike ʿAmr": you make the verb govern, affirmed and negated, in one and the same way. It is as if He said: "you are not mad, being favoured with that". The bāʾ did not prevent مجنون from governing what precedes it, because it is redundant, to emphasise the negation.» Most of the exegetes followed al-Zamakhsharī. Al-Nasafī said: «The bāʾ is attached to something omitted, its position is the accusative as a ḥāl, and what governs it is بمجنون.»
Abū Ḥayyān followed up al-Zamakhsharī on what he held, saying: «What al-Zamakhsharī held — that بنعمة ربك is attached to مجنون and that it is in the position of a ḥāl — requires reflection. That is because when negation bears upon a predicate that has a dependent, there are two ways: one is that the negation bears upon that dependent only; the other is that the negation bears upon the predicate, so its dependent is negated through its negation. To explain: you say "Zayd is not standing hastily", and what springs to mind is that his haste is negated, not his standing, so he stood without haste. The other way is that his standing is negated, so his haste is negated, i.e. there is no standing and therefore no haste. With what we have established, al-Zamakhsharī's statement cannot hold in any way; rather it leads to what is not permissible to utter concerning the one protected from error ﷺ.
2- The author of al-Mughnī mentioned that the bāʾ in «بأيّكم المفتون» is redundant. He said, among the places of the redundant bāʾ: «The third is the mubtadaʾ, and that is in their saying بحسبك درهم, and خرجت فإذا بزيد, and كيف بك إذا كان كذا وكذا; and among it, according to Sībawayh: بأيّكم المفتون. Abū al-Ḥasan said: بأيّكم is attached to an omitted "being settled" which is predicated of المفتون. Then they differed: it was said that المفتون is a maṣdar in the sense of الفتنة, and it was said that the bāʾ is locative, i.e. in which party of you is the afflicted one.»
Further, Abū Ḥayyān said: «It should not be taken in that way, because of its rarity.» For what is well known is that the bāʾ is not added to the mubtadaʾ, as a regular rule, except when it is the word «حسب». Ibn Yaʿīsh said: «As for its addition to the mubtadaʾ, it is in a single place, which is بحسبك.» Al-Kāfiyajī mentioned: «Its addition in بحسبك is an addition to the khabar; he made درهم a postponed mubtadaʾ and بحسبك the khabar, because it is the focus of the information, and the meaning is: one dirham is sufficient for you.» His student al-Suyūṭī said: «This is of considerable merit, and I know of nothing among his preferred views in Arabic better than it.» The justification [for an indefinite mubtadaʾ] in that case is the fronting of the khabar, which is a preposition and its genitive noun.

dervis-irab:8-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُدْهِنُ) The origin of الإدهان is softness, flattery and accommodation in speech. Al-Zamakhsharī placed it in Asās al-Balāgha among the figurative uses, saying: «Among the figurative uses: أدهن في الأمر and داهن: he flattered and was soft.»
(هَمَّازٍ) a fault-finder, i.e. a backbiter. It is also said that الهمّاز is the one who jabs people with his hand and strikes them, and اللمّاز (the one who does so) with the tongue. In al-Mukhtār: «اللمز is finding fault; its origin is signalling with the eye and the like; its pattern is that of ضرب and نصر, and it was read with both in the saying of the Exalted: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات. A man لمّاز and لمزة, on the measure of همزة, i.e. a fault-finder.» And in it also: «الهمز is like اللمز in measure and meaning; its pattern is that of ضرب. الهامز and الهمّاز are the fault-finder, and الهمزة is the same; one says a man همزة and a woman همزة too. The همزات of Satan are his whisperings, which he makes occur in a person's heart. المهماز is a piece of iron at the back of the horse-breaker's boot (a spur).»
(مَشَّاءٍ) an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha), i.e. one who goes about carrying words between people in order to corrupt relations between them.
(بِنَمِيمٍ) النميم: it is said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) like النميمة, and it is said to be a generic noun for it, like تمرة and تمر. It is conveying speech that displeases the one who hears it and stirs up people against one another, to kindle the fire of hatred in the breasts. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نمّ الرجل الحديث نمّا, from the patterns of قتل and ضرب: he carried it about to cause discord or estrangement; the man is نمّ, named by the maṣdar, and نمّام is intensive; the noun is النميمة, and النميم also.» Al-Zamakhsharī said:
النميم and النميمة are talebearing, and one of the Arabs recited to me:
تشبّبي تشبّب النميمة ... تمشي بها زهر إلى تميمه
(Blaze up as the talebearing blazes up, that Zahr carries to Tamīma.)
The verse al-Zamakhsharī cited as evidence is by a Bedouin addressing the fire. التشبّب is blazing; النميمة is falsifying speech and embellishing it to corrupt relations between people — a garment منمنم and منمّم is one that is decorated and beautified. Zahr is the name of a woman famous for talebearing, and Tamīma is a well-known tribe. He treated the fire as a rational being, commanded it and said: blaze up as the talebearing blazes up while this woman carries it to the Banū Tamīm. She used to do a great deal of mischief among the Arabs, until she became proverbial. Between نميمة and تميمة there is the "adjoining" paronomasia (al-jinās al-lāḥiq).
(مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ) i.e. miserly with wealth; الخير here is meant in the general sense of everything it applies to.
(عُتُلٍّ) coarse and harsh — it is said in nature, and it is said in body. Abū ʿUbayda said: he is the obscene, base one. It is also said: the coarse, harsh one. One says عتلته and عتنته (I dragged him roughly).
(زَنِيمٍ) one of doubtful lineage (daʿiyy). Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
وأنت زنيم نيط في آل هاشم ... كما نيط خلف الراكب القدح الفرد
(And you are a hanger-on attached to the family of Hāshim, as the single empty cup is hung behind the rider.)
With this verse Ḥassān addresses al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, saying that he is زنيم, i.e. hanging on the family of Hāshim like the زنمة on a hide, which is a small piece of skin left hanging at its edge; he likened him to it, and likened him to the single, empty cup hung behind the rider. Al-Walīd was of doubtful lineage in Quraysh, not of their stock; his father claimed him eighteen [Translator's note: the counted noun — days, months or years — is not specified in the source] after his birth. It is also said that his mother committed fornication, and this was not known until this verse was revealed. He made his harshness and his doubtful lineage the worst of his faults, because when he is harsh and coarse his heart hardens and he dares every act of disobedience, and because generally, when the sperm-drop is corrupt, what grows from it is corrupt; hence it came in the ḥadīth: «The child of fornication shall not enter Paradise, nor his child, nor his child's child.» It is related that when it was revealed, al-Walīd said to his mother: Muhammad has described me with nine attributes; I recognise them except the ninth of them, and if you do not tell me the truth I will strike off your head. She said to him:
"Your father was impotent, and I feared for the wealth, so I gave myself to the shepherd, and you are from him." This is what the exegetes said. What we hold — and Abū Ḥayyān preferred it — is that these descriptions are not of a specific person. Do you not see His words كل حلّاف? The prohibition only concerns obeying whoever has these attributes, which came for hyperbole. Further discussion of them will come in the section on rhetoric.
(سَنَسِمُهُ) We will put the mark on the face.
(الْخُرْطُومِ) the nose of beasts of prey; it is mostly used for the nose of the elephant and the pig. In al-Qāmūs: «الخرطوم, like زنبور, is the nose, or its front, or what you enclose between the two jaws, like الخرطم; the hedgehog.»

* I'rab:
(فَلا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied clause), because it conjoins to something omitted that the context indicates and that what precedes reveals. The prohibition serves to rouse and to inflame resolve in disobeying them. لا is prohibitive, and تطع is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the agent is latent (mustatir), implied as أنت, and المكذبين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ) ودّوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural. لو is a maṣdar-forming particle for wishing, in the view of the Basrans, because it comes after a verb of wishing; it was discussed in detail at the saying of the Exalted «يودّ أحدهم لو يعمّر ألف سنة». It, with what falls within its scope, is equivalent to a maṣdar, the object of ودّوا. It is also said that the object of ودّوا is omitted, i.e. "they wished for your compromising", and it was omitted because what follows indicates it, and لو remains in its usual role of being a particle for what would have happened on account of something else happening; its answer is then omitted, its implied form being "they would have been delighted at that". The fāʾ is a conjunction and يدهنون is an imperfect verb conjoined to تدهن, so it is within the scope of لو and is part of what is wished for; what is wished for is two things, the second caused by the first. Or it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. فهم يدهنون. In al-Kashshāf: «If you say: why was فيدهنون put in the nominative and not in the accusative by an implied أن, when it is the answer to the wish? I say: it was diverted to another path, namely that it was made the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. فهم يدهنون.» (وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَهِينٍ) the wāw is a conjunction, لا prohibitive, تطع an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا, كل حلّاف a mafʿūl bihi, and مهين a naʿt (adjective) for حلّاف. (هَمَّازٍ مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ) attributes listed in succession, which will be discussed in the section on rhetoric; بنميم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to مشّاء, and للخير is attached to منّاع. (عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ زَنِيمٍ) the adverb is attached to زنيم. This "afterness" is in rank, i.e. this description, زنيم, comes after the preceding attributes in rank and in hideousness; so بعد here is like the ثم that is for sequence and distance in rank. (أَنْ كانَ ذا مالٍ وَبَنِينَ) أن is maṣdariyya, and it, with what falls within its scope, is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-naziʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. لأن كان. It is attached to what إذا تتلى indicates, i.e. "he denied them". It cannot be governed by the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), because إذا is annexed to the clause after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes the muḍāf; nor can it be governed by قال, which is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because what comes after the conditional particle does not govern what precedes it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is attached to His words ولا تطع, meaning: do not obey him, with these faults, because he had wealth, i.e. on account of his affluence and his share of this world.» Abū Ḥayyān said: «It may be attached to what follows it, in the sense: because of his being wealthy and supported by sons, he denied Our signs.» كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; its subject is latent, implied as هو, ذا مال is its khabar, and بنين is conjoined to مال. (إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of a condition, attached to its answer; the clause تتلى عليه is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and the clause قال has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. أساطير الأولين is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. هي أساطير الأولين. (سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ) a resumptive clause; it is as if, having mentioned the vileness of his deeds and words, He mentioned what will be done to him by way of threat. The sīn is a particle of the future, نسمه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi, and على الخرطوم is attached to نسمه.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the coming of these attributes listed in a wondrous, captivating arrangement there is the device of correspondence (al-munāsaba). حلّاف came, and after it مهين, because the nūn in it with the mīm has ease [Translator's note: so in the source, «تراخ»]; then came همّاز مشّاء بنميم with the two intensive attributes; then came منّاع للخير معتد أثيم. After what He enumerated of his faults and defects, He brought two attributes that are among his worst failings, and the "afterness" (بعد) indicated that.
2- In His words «سنسمه على الخرطوم» there is a metonymy (kināya) for abasement and the lowest depths of humiliation. Since the face is the noblest part of a person, and the nose the most honoured part of the face, they made it the seat of might and pride, and derived from it الأنفة (disdain); among their sayings:
حمي الأنف شامخ العرنين
(proud of nose, lofty of nasal bridge)
and they said of the abased man: "his nose was cut off" and "his nose was rubbed in the dust". It was also, because of its prominence, among the places where brands show. He said سنسمه على الخرطوم, and that is the utmost in abasement, humiliation and stupefaction, since he becomes like a beast, unable to prevent being branded on the nose. If branding on the face is a disfigurement, how much more so on the most honoured organ in it? It has been said: beauty is in the nose. One of them said:
وحسن الفتى في الأنف والأنف عاطل ... فكيف إذا ما الخال كان له حليا
(A young man's beauty is in the nose, even when the nose is unadorned; so how much more when the mole is an ornament for it!)
Al-Rāzī made it a metaphor (istiʿāra): he borrowed الخرطوم for the nose; I see no suitability in it. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl strained the meaning, saying that الخرطوم is wine and that he will be given the prescribed punishment for drinking it. This is the extreme of forced interpretation, even if الخرطوم is among the names of wine; wine was called الخرطوم because it flies up into the nostrils.

dervis-irab:17-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَلَوْناهُمْ) We tried them and tested them.
(لَيَصْرِمُنَّها) الصرم is cutting; what is meant is that they would cut its fruit. One says صرم العذق عن النخلة (he cut the cluster from the palm), and أصرم النخل, i.e. the time for cutting it has come, like أركب المهر and أحصد الزرع, i.e. the time for riding it and harvesting it has come. In al-Mukhtār: «صرم النخل: he cut it; its pattern is that of ضرب. أصرم النخل: the time came for it to be cut. الانصرام is being cut off, التصارم is mutual severance, and التصرّم is breaking off.»
(طائِفٌ) Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the matter that comes by night. He was refuted by the saying of the Exalted «إذا مسّهم طائف من الشيطان», for that is not specific to night or day; but it is predominantly used for evil.
(الصريم) It is said to be night of intense darkness. Night was called صريم because it is cut off and separated from the day and severed from it, just as the day is also called صريم because it is cut off from the night. It also has many other meanings, among them: an orchard whose fruits have been cut so that nothing remains in it, so it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle); and a huge tract of sand cut off from the rest of the sands.
(يَتَخافَتُونَ) they speak secretly among themselves. خفي, خفت and خفد, all three, are in the sense of concealing.
(حَرْدٍ) withholding, or purpose; and الحرد with the middle letter voweled is anger. In al-Mukhtār:
«حرد: he aimed; its pattern is that of خرب [Translator's note: so in the source]. The saying of the Exalted «وغدوا على حرد قادرين» means: upon purpose; it is also said: upon withholding. الحرد with the middle letter voweled is anger. Abū Naṣr, the companion of al-Aṣmaʿī, said it is with the middle letter unvoweled, so on this view its pattern is that of فهم; Ibn al-Sikkīt said it may be voweled, so on this view its pattern is that of طرب, and he is حارد and حردان.» In al-Samīn: الحرد has many views: it is said to be anger and rage; it is said to be withholding, from حاردت الإبل, meaning the camels' milk became little, and حاردت السنة, meaning the year's water became little — Abū ʿUbayd said this; one says حرد with kasra, يحرد, حردا, and it may be given a fatḥa, so one says حرد, and he is حردان and حارد; one says أسد حارد (an angry lion) and ليوث حوارد (angry lions). It is said that الحرد and الحرد [Translator's note: the two vowelings are not distinguished in the source text] are being alone; one says حرد with fatḥa, يحرد with ḍamma, حرودا and حردا, and حرد meaning he withdrew; from it كوكب حارد, or solitary. It is also said that الحرد is purpose; one says حرد حردك, i.e. he aimed at your aim.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّا بَلَوْناهُمْ كَما بَلَوْنا أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّها مُصْبِحِينَ) إنّ and its subject; the clause بلوناهم is its khabar (predicate), and it is a verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hāʾ refers to the people of Mecca. كما: the kāf is in the position of an accusative as the adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. بلوناهم بلاء; ما is maṣdariyya, and it is also said to be in the sense of الذي. إذ is a past adverb attached (mutaʿalliq) to بلونا, and the clause أقسموا is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The lām falls in the answer to the oath, and يصرمنّها is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the agent, i.e. ليصرموننها. مصبحين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of ليصرمنّها, and it is an active participle from the complete (tāmma) أصبح. (وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ) the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; لا is negating, and يستثنون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, i.e. they made no exception in their oaths. The wāw's being circumstantial is weak, inasmuch as the imperfect negated by لا is like the affirmative in that the wāw does not enter it — unless it is by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject) before it. The meaning of لا يستثنون is: they did not turn their resolve back from depriving [the poor]. It is also said: they did not say "if Allah the Exalted wills"; this was called an exception (istithnāʾ) although it is a condition, because the meaning of "I will certainly go out, if Allah wills" and "I will not go out unless Allah wills" is one. (فَطافَ عَلَيْها طائِفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَهُمْ نائِمُونَ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, طاف a past verb, عليها attached to it, طائف the agent, and من ربك a naʿt (adjective) for طائف; the wāw is circumstantial, هم a mubtadaʾ and نائمون the khabar. (فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, أصبحت a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose subject is latent (mustatir), implied as هي, and كالصريم the khabar. (فَتَنادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, تنادوا a past verb and its agent, and مصبحين a ḥāl; the clause is conjoined to أقسموا. (أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ) أن is explicative (mufassira), because it is preceded by something with the meaning of saying but not its letters. You may also make it maṣdariyya, so that it and what follows it are equivalent to a maṣdar in the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-naziʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. بأن أغدو [Translator's note: so in the source, for بأن اغدوا]. اغدوا is a defective imperative verb, the wāw is its subject, and على حرثكم is its khabar. It was made transitive with على because it contains the meaning of أقبلوا (come towards). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: why was it not said اغدوا إلى حرثكم, and what is the meaning of على? I say: since going out to it in the morning was in order to cut and sever it, it was a going out against it, as you say غدا عليهم العدو (the enemy came upon them in the morning). It may also be that الغدو is made to contain the meaning of الإقبال, as in their saying "the large bowl is brought to them (يغدى عليهم) morning and evening", i.e. so come early to your tillage.» Abū Ḥayyān rejected al-Zamakhsharī's first statement, saying: «Al-Zamakhsharī presupposed that غدا is made transitive with إلى; that needs to be transmitted, to the extent that it becomes frequent and so becomes its basic usage and whatever differs from it is interpreted. What I have memorised is that it is made transitive with على, as in the poet's saying:
بكرت عليه غدوة فرأيته ... قعودا عليه بالصريم عواذله
(I came to him early in the morning and found his reproachers sitting around him at al-Ṣarīm.)»
إن is conditional and its apodosis is omitted, i.e. "if you are truthful [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has صارمين], then go out early". (فَانْطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخافَتُونَ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, انطلقوا a past verb and its agent; the wāw is circumstantial, هم a mubtadaʾ and the clause يتخافتون the khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (أَنْ لا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِسْكِينٌ) أن is explicative or maṣdariyya; its parallel has been given before. لا is negating, and يدخلنّها is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). اليوم is an adverb attached to يدخلنّها, عليكم is also attached to يدخلنّها, and مسكين is the agent. (وَغَدَوْا عَلى حَرْدٍ قادِرِينَ) the wāw is a conjunction, غدوا a defective past verb and the wāw its subject; على حرد is attached to قادرين, and قادرين is the khabar of غدوا. It is permissible for غدوا to be complete (tāmma), with قادرين a ḥāl from the agent of غدوا and على حرد attached to it; or for على حرد to be the ḥāl and قادرين a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the first ḥāl, making it an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). (فَلَمَّا رَأَوْها قالُوا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ) the fāʾ is a conjunction and لمّا is temporal (ḥīniyya) or a linking particle; the clause رأوها is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and رأوها is a verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi. The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. إنّ and its subject, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ضالّون its khabar; إنّ with its subject and khabar is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). (بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ) بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction, نحن a mubtadaʾ and محرومون the khabar. (قالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلا تُسَبِّحُونَ) قال is a past verb and أوسطهم its agent; the meaning of أوسطهم is the best and most sensible of them. The hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal (inkār); لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive, and أقل an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم. لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e. هلّا (why not); تسبحون is an imperfect verb and its agent, and its object is omitted, i.e. Allah, and that is by repenting to Him. (قالُوا سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ) قالوا is a past verb and its agent; سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and ربنا a muḍāf ilayhi. إنّ and its subject, the clause كنّا its khabar, and ظالمين the khabar of كنّا. The clause إنّا كنّا gives the reason for the glorification; through it they confessed their wrongdoing in withholding kindness and omitting the exception. (فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَلاوَمُونَ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, أقبل بعضهم a past verb and its agent, على بعض attached to أقبل, and the clause يتلاومون a ḥāl. (قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا طاغِينَ) يا is a vocative particle and ويلنا an annexed one addressed (munādā muḍāf). They called woe upon themselves, i.e. "O our woe, this is the time for you to come to us, for you are now our resort and our last resource". إنّ and its subject, the clause كنّا its khabar, and طاغين the khabar of كنّا. (عَسى رَبُّنا أَنْ يُبْدِلَنا خَيْراً مِنْها إِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا راغِبُونَ) عسى is a defective past verb, one of the verbs of hope; ربنا is its subject, and أن with what falls within its scope is its khabar; خيرا is a second object. إنّ and its subject; إلى ربنا is attached to راغبون, and راغبون is the khabar of إنّا. They hoped that Allah would accept their repentance and give them in exchange something better than their garden. (كَذلِكَ الْعَذابُ وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ) كذلك is a fronted khabar and العذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. The lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), عذاب الآخرة a mubtadaʾ and أكبر the khabar. لو is conditional; كان and its subject, and the clause يعلمون its khabar. The answer of لو is omitted, indicated by the context of the speech, its implied form being: "what they did before — the wrongdoing and the refraining from making the exception — would not have come from them."

* Rhetoric:
In His words «فطاف عليها طائف من ربك» طائف is indefinite, and the benefit of that is vagueness, to magnify what befell their garden. The meaning of كالصريم is: because of the destruction of its fruit. It is also said that الصريم is the night, because it was burnt and turned black; and it is said: the day, because it became empty and bare — and from this comes the "whiteness" of the land, i.e. land empty of trees. The meaning of صارمين is harvesting, and the meaning of يتخافتون is: they spoke their talk secretly for fear that the poor would come upon them. الحرد is from حاردت السنة, when the year withholds its good; the meaning is: they went out early upon hardship and withholding. It is also said that الحرد is speed, i.e. they went out early, hastening and brisk, to the deprivation they had resolved upon. He said:
أقبل سيل جاء من أمر الله ... يحرد حرد الجنة المغلة
(A flood came forward, coming by Allah's command, speeding as the fruitful garden speeds.)
He is describing a flood as abundant. The alif before the hāʾ was dropped from the word of Majesty because that is permissible in pausing. The meaning of يحرد حرد الجنة المغلة is: it speeds as the garden — i.e. the orchard — المغلة, i.e. abundant in produce and good, speeds; and its speeding is the appearance of its good before others in a short time, because of the flood that came upon it suddenly and made it lush and fertile.

dervis-irab:34-43.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ) إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; للمتقين is its fronted khabar (predicate); عند ربهم: the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from جنات, or attached to the "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; جنات النعيم is the postponed subject of إنّ. The clause is resumptive, introduced to explain what Allah has prepared for the God-fearing on the Day of Resurrection, and to answer the leaders of Quraysh who used to say: if it is true that we will be resurrected, our state and the state of the believers will be nothing but what it is in this world. (أَفَنَجْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ) the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal (inkār) and the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "shall We be unjust in judgement and make the Muslims like the disbelievers?" نجعل is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its agent latent (mustatir), المسلمين the first object, and كالمجرمين in the position of the second object. This is the first rebuke and reproach of the disbelievers, and five other rebukes will follow it. (ما لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ) this is the second reproach. ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لكم the khabar; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, and تحكمون an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is circumstantial, and it is the third reproach. (أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ) أم is a conjunction for transitional turning away (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī), and the hamza contained within it is for the interrogative of disavowal and rebuke; this is the fourth reproach. لكم is a fronted khabar and كتاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; فيه is attached to تدرسون, and تدرسون is an imperfect verb in the nominative with its agent; the clause تدرسون is circumstantial or resumptive. (إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ) the clause is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of تدرسون, because it is what is studied. The apparent form would have been to give the hamza of أنّ a fatḥa, but since the lām that is specific to the kasra form was brought, it was given a kasra, and it suspended the verb from governing the wording of the clause; suspension (taʿlīq) entered it even though studying is one of the verbs of the heart, because it contains the meaning of judging [Translator's note: so in the source, «وإن الدرس من أفعال القلوب»; the sense appears to be that دَرَس is treated as a verb of the heart because it contains the meaning of judging]. لكم is the fronted khabar of إنّ, فيه a ḥāl, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) was brought for emphasis; ما is the postponed subject of إنّ and the clause تخيرون its ṣila (relative clause). The original form of تخيرون is تتخيرون, in the sense of تختارون (you choose). (أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمانٌ عَلَيْنا بالِغَةٌ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ) this is the fifth reproach. لكم is a fronted khabar and أيمان a postponed mubtadaʾ; علينا is an adjective for أيمان and بالغة a second adjective. إلى يوم القيامة is attached to the "being settled" to which the khabar, namely لكم, is attached, or to بالغة, i.e. reaching to that Day and ending at it. In His words أم لكم etc. there is the meaning of an oath, as if it were said: "have We sworn to you binding oaths?" (إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَما تَحْكُمُونَ) the clause is the answer to the oath that is in view, so it has no grammatical position. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, لكم its fronted khabar, the shifted lām is for emphasis, ما is the postponed subject of إنّ, and the clause تحكمون is the ṣila. (سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ بِذلِكَ زَعِيمٌ) the clause is resumptive. سل is an imperative verb, its latent agent, and its first object; أيّهم is a mubtadaʾ, بذلك is attached to زعيم, and زعيم is the khabar of أيّهم; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the second object of سل, because it takes two objects, and it was suspended from governing by the interrogative, which is the sixth reproach. (أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكاءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ إِنْ كانُوا صادِقِينَ) this is the seventh reproach [Translator's note: the source earlier announced the first reproach followed by "five other rebukes", i.e. six in all, but it numbers seven here and in the Rhetoric section]. لهم is a fronted khabar and شركاء a postponed mubtadaʾ; this clause is conjoined in meaning to the clause أيّهم بذلك زعيم. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it reveals an implied condition, the implied form being "if that is so, then let them bring". The lām is the lām of command; يأتوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām and the wāw is the agent; بشركائهم is attached to يأتوا. إن is conditional; كانوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw its subject and صادقين its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what preceded, i.e. "then let them bring their partners". (يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ) the adverb is a mafʿūl bihi of an implied اذكر (remember), or it is attached to His words فليأتوا. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «What puts the adverb in the accusative is فليأتوا, or an implied اذكر, or "on the day the shin is bared, such-and-such will happen", omitted for eloquent intimidation.» The clause يكشف is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; يكشف is in the passive, and عن ساق stands in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ويدعون: the wāw is a conjunction, and يدعون is a passive imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; إلى السجود is attached to يدعون. The fāʾ is a conjunction, لا is negating, and يستطيعون is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the agent. (خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ) خاشعة is a ḥāl from the pronoun of يدعون, i.e. humbled, and أبصارهم is the agent of خاشعة; the clause ترهقهم is a second ḥāl, ترهقهم being an imperfect verb with a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and ذلّة a postponed agent. (وَقَدْ كانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سالِمُونَ) the wāw is circumstantial, قد a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), كانوا a defective past verb and the wāw its subject; the clause يدعون is the khabar of كانوا, and إلى السجود is attached to يدعون. The wāw is circumstantial, هم a mubtadaʾ and سالمون the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative of disavowal and reproach: it was stated in the i'rab that the interrogatives occurring in these verses are seven. They have departed from their original meaning to disavowal, rebuke and reproach for the rumours they spread in claiming: "Allah has favoured us over you in this world, so He must favour us over you in the Hereafter; or at least, if the favouring does not happen, then nothing less than equality." So Allah refuted their feeble claims, reproaching and rebuking, and they came in succession: the first is أفنجعل, the second ما لكم, the third كيف تحكمون, the fourth أم لكم كتاب, the fifth أم لكم أيمان, the sixth أيّهم بذلك زعيم, and the seventh أم لهم شركاء. They are strung on a thread of eloquence and clarity before which every eloquence bows.
2- In His words «يوم يكشف عن ساق» there is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). The origin of this expression is that it is said of one who tucks up his garment from his shin during hard work, because whoever falls into something requiring earnestness tucks up his garment from his shin; so the shin and baring it were borrowed for the severity of the matter. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «Baring the shin and revealing the anklets are a proverbial expression for the severity of a matter and the difficulty of an affair. Its origin is in terror and rout, and secluded women tucking up their garments from their shins in flight and revealing their anklets at that time.»
Al-Zamakhsharī's saying "revealing الخدام": it is the plural of خدمة, which is the anklet, like رقاب, plural of رقبة. Ḥātim said:
أخو الحرب إن غصّت به الحرب عضّها ... وإن شمّرت عن ساقها الحرب شمّرا
(The brother of war: if war chokes on him, he bites it; and if war tucks up its garment from its shin, he tucks up his.)
And Ibn al-Ruqayyāt said:
تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدي ... عن خدام العقيلة العذراء
(It makes the old man forget his sons, and lays bare the anklets of the noble virgin.)
Tucking up from the shin is a metonymy (kināya) for the intensification and difficulty of a matter. Its origin is to attribute it to a human being, because the garment is tucked up from the shin to wade into deep water, or to run, or the like; it was attributed to war by likening war to a human being, by way of metaphor. As for the second verse, before it comes:
كيف نومي على الفراش ولما ... تشمل الشام غارة شعواء
تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدي ... عن خدام العقيلة العذراء
(How can I sleep on my bed when a widespread raid has not yet engulfed Syria, one that makes the old man forget his sons and lays bare the anklets of the noble virgin?)
الخدام is the anklet; العقيلة is the noble woman — the عقيلة of everything is its most precious — and, among women, the secluded one who is kept within her curtained chamber.
3- In making ساق indefinite there is vagueness for hyperbole, indicating that it is a matter obscure in its severity, unfamiliar, outside what is customary and usual.
4- In attributing humility to the eyes there is a rational figure of speech (majāz ʿaqlī), because what is in the heart is known from the eye.

dervis-irab:44-52.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ) We will take them little by little. One says استدرجه إلى كذا:
he brought him near to it, raised him from step to step, and made him advance gradually on the ground. Al-Khaṭīb said: «سنستدرجهم, i.e. We will take them, by Our majesty, gradually, not by surprise, into a punishment about which there is no doubt.»
(مَكْظُومٌ) filled with grief or distress. Al-Māwardī said: «The difference between them is that grief (الغم) is in the heart and distress (الكرب) is in the breaths.» It is also said: مكظوم means confined, الكظم being confinement. Al-Mubarrad said: «He is the one seized by his كظم, which is the passage of the breath.»
(لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصارِهِمْ) i.e. they look at you with an intense look that almost throws you down and makes you fall from your place.

* I'rab:
(فَذَرْنِي وَمَنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the command follow on from what preceded of their states as narrated. You may also make it the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition), because it is the answer to an implied condition, the implied form being "since their states are thus, leave Me". ذر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), implied as أنت, referring to the Messenger ﷺ; the yāʾ is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is a conjunction and من is conjoined to the yāʾ; or the wāw is for accompaniment and من is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the first is preferable. The clause يكذب is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; بهذا is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يكذب, and الحديث is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative. (سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) resumptive speech, introduced to explain the manner of the punishment conveyed in summary by the preceding command. The pronoun refers to من, and the plural is with regard to its meaning, just as the singular in يكذب is with regard to its wording. نستدرجهم is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; من is a preposition and حيث an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of a genitive by من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نستدرجهم, and the clause لا يعلمون is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. (وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ) the wāw is a conjunction, and أملي is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, implied as أنا, because it is conjoined to سنستدرجهم; لهم is attached to أملي. الإملاء is granting respite and following up favours and blessings so that they will be deluded; the explanation of this figure of speech will come in the section on rhetoric. إنّ with its subject and its khabar (predicate); the clause serves as the reason for the granting of respite. (أَمْ تَسْئَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ) conjoined to what preceded in His words أم لهم شركاء, i.e. "or do you seek from them a recompense for the guidance and faith to which you call them?" تسألهم is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a first object, and أجرا a second object. The fāʾ is a conjunction, هم a mubtadaʾ (subject), من مغرم attached to مثقلون, and مثقلون the khabar, i.e. burdened with a heavy load under which they stagger. (أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) also conjoined. عندهم is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and الغيب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم a mubtadaʾ and the clause يكتبون the khabar. (فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نادى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; اصبر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, implied as أنت, and لحكم ربك is attached to اصبر. The wāw is a conjunction, لا prohibitive, and تكن an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; its subject is latent, implied as أنت, and كصاحب الحوت is the khabar — meaning Yūnus, upon him be peace, whose story has been told before. إذ is an adverb in the accusative by an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "let not your state be like his state, nor your story like his story, at the time of his calling out". The meaning is: let there not be found in you what was found in him of vexation and leaving in anger, so that you would be tried with his trial. The clause نادى is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ and مكظوم the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of نادى. (لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ) لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence, containing the sense of a condition; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; تداركه is a past verb and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi, and نعمة is the agent; the verb was made masculine because the femininity of نعمة is not real. من ربه is a naʿt (adjective) for نعمة. أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is obligatorily omitted. The lām falls in the answer of لولا; نبذ is a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as هو; بالعراء is attached to نبذ, i.e. on the open, barren land. The wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ and مذموم the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun of نبذ. (فَاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. "so a favour from his Lord reached him, and He chose him". اجتباه [Translator's note: the source prints «واجتباره»] is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi, and ربه its agent, i.e. He gathered him to Himself and brought him near by accepting his repentance. فجعله is conjoined to فاجتباه; the hāʾ is the first object and من الصالحين is in the position of the second object. (وَإِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ) the wāw is resumptive; إن is lightened from the heavy (inna), and its subject is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), or — more likely — it is inoperative (muhmala). يكاد is an imperfect verb from the verbs of approximation, الذين its subject, and the clause كفروا the ṣila. The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); يزلقونك is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the agent and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; بأبصارهم is attached to يزلقونك. لمّا is a linking particle or a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya ẓarfiyya); سمعوا is a verb and its agent, and الذكر a mafʿūl bihi. The meaning is that, from the intensity of their staring and casting sidelong glances at you, they almost make your foot slip, or destroy you. He said:
يتقارضون إذا التقوا في موطن ... نظرا يزل مواطىء الأقدام
(When they meet in a place they exchange looks that make the footholds of the feet slip.)
The answer of لمّا is omitted because it is indicated, i.e. "when they heard the Reminder, they almost made you slip". (وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ) the wāw is a conjunction and يقولون is conjoined to يزلقونك; إنّ and its subject, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مجنون its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of their saying. (وَما هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ) the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negating and inoperative because the negation is broken by إلا; هو is a mubtadaʾ, إلا a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), ذكر the khabar of هو, and للعالمين a naʿt for ذكر.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين» there is a non-metaphorical figure (majāz mursal): He called His granting them respite and following up favours and blessings upon them "a plot" (kayd), because it is the cause of entanglement and destruction; for the reality of plotting is a kind of stratagem, and a stratagem is to do what is outwardly beneficial and good while you intend its opposite. What came about of the ampleness of their provision, the ease of their living and the length of their lives is outwardly beneficence towards them, while what is intended by it is harm and destruction.
2- In His words «وهو مذموم» there is also a majāz mursal, because blame is in reality a cause of censure, so the relation is causality. Fine is the saying of al-Rāzī: «"And he is blameworthy", in respect of his being a doer of a sin [Translator's note: so in the source; the objection being raised is that the verse implies he committed a sin]. He said: the answer is from three aspects: first, that the word لولا indicates that this blameworthiness did not come about; second, perhaps what is meant by blameworthiness is the abandoning of what is better, for the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near; third, perhaps this event was before prophethood.» Taking the verse figuratively is more fitting than straining after these possibilities.
